name: Caprese Sandwich
steps: Check that the ciabatta contains eggless and the fresh mozzarella uses vegetarian coagulants. Slice the bread rolls horizontally. Pat mozzarella slices and tomato slices dry with a clean towel so the bread does not become soggy.
Warm the cut sides of the ciabatta in a dry pan for 1–2 minutes until lightly crisp but still soft inside. Rub or brush the cut surfaces with most of the measured olive oil.
Layer tomato slices over the bottom halves and season with the measured salt and black pepper. Add mozzarella slices and generous whole basil leaves, distributing them evenly across all four rolls.
Drizzle balsamic glaze over the filling and add the remaining olive oil. Close the rolls gently without squeezing out the filling.
Cut each sandwich in half with a sharp serrated knife so the tomato, mozzarella and basil layers remain clear. Serve immediately at room temperature while the basil is fresh and bread crisp.
tips: Fresh mozzarella can release water, so drain it before assembly. The reviewed photo shows rustic ciabatta, thick white mozzarella, ripe red tomato, basil, olive oil and a little dark balsamic glaze.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
